features.name: Content hosting
features.summary: Release 17 M1 provisioning of sessions, server certificates and content hosting, HTTP pull ingest with an HTTP(S) cache, Service Access Information and DASH playback work, with a 202 on session delete, no PATCH, a faulty purge reply, and no caching rules, URL signing, geofencing, push or low-latency delivery; none of the Release 19 APIs exist, M3 is a 5G-MAG pre-standard API, and the specifications disagree on how path rewrite rules match and on the deprecated pull identifier.

requirements.name: M1 Content Protocols Discovery

cases.case: Fetch list of supported content protocols (GET .../protocols)
cases.what: Answers GET on the protocols sub-resource of an existing Provisioning Session with 200 and an application/json ContentProtocols document; an unknown session gets 404.
Lists one downlink ingest protocol, urn:3gpp:5gms:content-protocol:http-pull-ingest, with a descriptionLocator, which is the only protocol the 5GMS AS accepts.
The document omits geoFencingLocatorTypes, and no geofencing locator type is supported anywhere in the system; the clause requires every 5GMS System to support at least the ISO 3166 locator type.

noted: The ContentProtocols document is fixed at build time and is the same for every Provisioning Session, including uplink ones; it is not derived from the Application Servers actually configured.

requirements.name: M1 Provisioning Sessions

cases.what: Creates a session from provisioningSessionType, appId and optional aspId, rejects a missing or malformed field with 400, and answers 201 with a Location header ending in the new identifier and the ProvisioningSession body.

Returns 200 with the ProvisioningSession JSON (provisioningSessionId, provisioningSessionType, appId, aspId and the lists of certificate, metrics reporting and policy template identifiers); 404 for an unknown or deleted session.
Removes the session and its configurations but answers 202 Accepted; the V17.10.0 OpenAPI defines 204 No Content as the only success response.
Each list is filled from what is provisioned in the session and left out when empty.

noted: provisioningSessionType is stored but no behaviour depends on it; an UPLINK session is handled like a downlink one.
contentPreparationTemplateIds, edgeResourcesConfigurationIds and eventDataProcessingConfigurationIds are never present because those resources cannot be provisioned.
The Location value is the request URI as received by the AF with the identifier appended; whether that URI is absolute depends on the HTTP library and was not checked.

requirements.name: M1 Server Certificates

cases.what: Generates a certificate for the AS canonical host name, or reuses one already held for that host name, and answers 200 with a Location header naming the certificate resource.
With the csr query parameter, accepts an empty body or a JSON array of domain name aliases, answers 200 with a Location header and an application/x-pem-file Certificate Signing Request.
cases.locator: clause 7.3.2, Table 7.3.2-1, row Reserve Server Certificate

cases.what: Returns 200 with the PEM certificate, 204 when the certificate is reserved but not yet uploaded, and 404 when the identifier is not in the session.
cases.locator: clause 7.3.2, Table 7.3.2-1, row Retrieve Server Certificate

cases.what: Accepts only application/x-pem-file (415 otherwise), checks the certificate against the key generated with the CSR (400 on mismatch or when no CSR exists), answers 204, and rejects a second upload with 403.
cases.locator: clause 7.3.2, Table 7.3.2-1, row Upload Server Certificate

cases.what: Deletes the certificate and answers 204, or 404 when it does not exist.
Responses carry only the PEM certificate or the CSR; the key generated alongside the CSR is never returned at M1.

noted: The certificate is always issued for the first Application Server in the AF configuration.
A body sent with Create (without csr) is ignored rather than rejected; the clause says that body shall be empty.
The clause calls a second upload an error without naming a status code; the AF uses 403.

cases.case: Content Preparation Templates API (create, retrieve, update, destroy)
cases.what: No content-preparation-templates sub-resource exists and none is generated from the OpenAPI files; requests to it get 404 as an unknown sub-resource.

requirements.name: M1 Content Hosting Provisioning

cases.what: Parses and validates the ContentHostingConfiguration, stores it, queues it for the AS over M3 and answers 201 with a Location header and the stored configuration; malformed input gets 400.
Returns 200 with the stored configuration including the AF-assigned fields, or 404 when none exists.
Replaces the configuration, pushes the change to the AS and answers 204; malformed input gets 400.
PATCH is not handled for any M1 resource; it falls through to a 403 Forbidden answer. Clause 7.6.2 allows PATCH and the OpenAPI defines it with a 200 response.
cases.locator: clause 7.6.2, Table 7.6.2-1, row Update Content Hosting Configuration; TS26512_M1_ContentHostingProvisioning.yaml, PATCH

cases.what: Removes the configuration from the AF and the AS and answers 204, or 404 when none exists.
Rejects any other Content-Type with 415 and forwards the body to each AS hosting the session.

cases.case: Purge result: 200 with total, or 204 when nothing was purged
cases.what: After the AS answers, the AF always replies 200 with the summed count, including a count of 0; the clause requires 204 No Content when no cache entries were purged.

cases.case: Purge with more than one session on the same AS
cases.what: While collecting the AS work, the AF sends a 500 error for every other Provisioning Session assigned to the same AS and then still sends the real result, so the request fails as soon as an AS hosts a second session; the clause expects one success response.

cases.case: Purge with a malformed regular expression
cases.what: The AF does not check the expression itself, but relays the 400 the AS returns for an expression that does not compile.
Sets canonicalDomainName of every distribution configuration to the canonical host name of the AS, overwriting any value supplied.

cases.case: Distribution baseURL chosen by the AF
cases.what: Builds a unique baseURL per session from the scheme (https when certificateId is set), the domainNameAlias or canonical host name, and the configured path prefix containing the session identifier.

cases.case: Input checks (ingest baseURL, entryPoint.relativePath, non-empty profiles, certificateId)
cases.what: Rejects a malformed ingest baseURL, a relativePath that is not relative, or an empty profiles array with 400; a certificateId not provisioned in the session gets 404 on create.

cases.case: Push ingest: ingest baseURL assigned by the AF
cases.what: For a push-based (dash-if-ingest) configuration the AF does not generate the ingest baseURL the Application Provider should upload to; it stores whatever was supplied.

noted: POST on a session that already has a Content Hosting Configuration replaces it and answers 201; PUT on a session without one creates it and answers 204.
The ingest protocol is not checked against the protocols the AF advertises, so a configuration the AS cannot serve is accepted at M1.
An Application Provider-supplied baseURL or canonicalDomainName is silently overwritten; the clause calls setting baseURL an error by the Application Provider without saying how the AF reacts.
The AF does not check that domainNameAlias matches a subjectAltName of the referenced certificate.
Only the first configured Application Server is used for every session.
On create, a certificateId that is not provisioned is reported with 404 after the configuration has already been stored.
The 204 answer to PUT carries a Content-Type and a Location header although it has no body.

requirements.name: M5 Service Access Information

cases.what: Answers GET with 200 and an application/json ServiceAccessInformation built for the session, with ETag, Last-Modified and Cache-Control headers; 404 for an unknown session.
Both are present; the type is always DOWNLINK, which is correct for the downlink sessions this feature covers.
Present only when a Content Hosting Configuration exists; each entry point carries a locator built from the distribution baseURL and relativePath, the contentType and any profiles.

noted: Conditional GET is supported: If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since produce 304 Not Modified.
eMBMSServiceAnnouncementLocator and clientEdgeResourcesConfiguration are never present, since neither eMBMS nor edge resources can be provisioned.
For an UPLINK Provisioning Session the resource still says DOWNLINK.

requirements.name: Content Hosting operations at the AS (caching, purge, URL signing, geofencing)

cases.case: Caching rules (cachingConfigurations: urlPatternFilter, first match, noCache, maxAge, statusCodeFilters)
cases.what: cachingConfigurations is accepted in the configuration but never turned into cache rules; every resource is cached the same way.

cases.case: Defaults when no rule matches and the origin gives no directives
cases.what: Uses fixed defaults for all resources (200 responses kept for one day, any other status for one minute); the clause requires defaults based on the media resource type.

cases.case: Origin HTTP header fields not forwarded by default
cases.what: The proxy configuration hides none of the origin's response header fields, so they are passed on at M4d; clause 7.6.4.2 says that by default origin header fields are not forwarded (the originCacheHeaders flag it names to change this is not defined in table 7.6.3.1-1).

On a purge request from the AF, deletes the cached entries of the session whose path matches the regular expression (all entries when none is given), reloads the proxy and returns the count, or 204 when nothing matched.

cases.case: Content processing from a Content Preparation Template
cases.what: contentPreparationTemplateId is ignored; no repackaging, encryption or transcoding is done.
urlSignature is accepted in the configuration but not applied; M4d requests are served without checking any URL signature.
geoFencing is accepted in the configuration but not applied.
Creates a virtual server for the alias host name with the same locations as the canonical one.
No CORS headers are added at M4d for the alias or any other origin.

cases.case: certificateId: TLS at M4d with the provisioned certificate
cases.what: A distribution with certificateId is served over HTTPS on the configured port using the certificate bundle received from the AF.

noted: Caching only happens when a cache directory is configured.
Deleting a Content Hosting Configuration also purges its cache entries.

requirements.name: M2d HTTP pull-based content ingest

cases.case: Protocol http-pull-ingest with pull set to true
cases.what: Accepts a configuration whose protocol is urn:3gpp:5gms:content-protocol:http-pull-ingest with pull true and requires an ingest baseURL.
Proxies to the ingest baseURL as given, so an https origin is fetched over TLS with server name indication.

cases.case: Step 1: replace the M4d baseURL prefix with the ingest baseURL
cases.what: Each distribution baseURL path becomes a proxy location whose requests are forwarded to the ingest baseURL followed by the rest of the path; a cache miss triggers the origin request.

cases.case: Step 2: path rewrite rules in order, first match only
cases.what: Each pathRewriteRule becomes a rewrite directive in list order that stops at the first match; the leaf path element is kept out of the comparison and carried over.

cases.case: Step 2: part of the request path a requestPathPattern is compared against
cases.what: Applies each rule to the whole M4d request path, including the leading "/" and the distribution baseURL path, with the leaf path element left out of the comparison; a pattern without a leading ^ may match anywhere in that path.
cases.conflict: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 8.2, step 2: "The path rewrite rules (if provisioned in DistributionConfiguration.PathRewriteRules) are applied in strict order to the remainder of the request URL (i.e., the path segments following Distribution‌Configuration.‌baseURL)." TS 26.512 V17.10.0 table 7.6.3.1-1, row pathRewriteRules.requestPathPattern (read from the .docx): "A regular expression [5] against which the path part of each 5GMSd AS request URL, including the leading "/", and up to and including the final "/", shall be compared."

cases.case: 3xx redirect from the origin mapped to a dynamic M4d endpoint
cases.what: 301, 302 and 307 from the origin are turned into a redirect to a generated M4d prefix whose requests are proxied to the redirect target; 303 and 308 are not intercepted and reach the player with the origin location, bypassing the AS.

noted: The origin URL is built from the base URL and the rewritten path only; the M4d query string is not added to it.
A single configuration with another protocol or with push ingest makes generation of the whole proxy configuration fail, which stops every session on that AS.

cases.what: There is no ingest endpoint; a configuration with dash-if-ingest or pull false is rejected when the proxy configuration is generated.

cases.case: Serve MPD and Segments at M4d
cases.what: Serves whatever the origin provides unchanged over HTTP or HTTPS from the cache, so MPD and Segment conformance is that of the origin content.

requirements.name: M5 Service Access Information

cases.what: The Media Session Handler requests the resource relative to the M5 base URL it was given and keeps the parsed result.
Uses the SAI entry points (locator, contentType, profiles) when the service list entry from the application has none.

The model declares streamingAccess as always present and the code reads it without a check, so a resource without it fails to be used when the application supplies no entry points; table 11.2.3.1-1 gives it cardinality 0..1.

noted: The resource is re-fetched on a timer derived from Cache-Control max-age, Age and Expires, with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since; a 304 keeps the previous copy.

eMBMSServiceAnnouncementLocator, dynamicPolicyInvocationConfiguration, networkAssistanceConfiguration and clientEdgeResourcesConfiguration are not modelled; they are assessed under their own features.

cases.case: 3xx redirect mapped to a dynamic M4d endpoint
cases.what: 301, 302 and 307 from the origin are turned into a redirect to a generated M4d prefix that is proxied to the redirect target; 303 and 308 reach the player with the origin location. Clause 8.2 requires an equivalent M4d redirect for any 3xx redirect.

features.name: M3 between AF and AS
features.summary: The AF and AS implement the 5G-MAG pre-standard M3 (/3gpp-m3/v1) for certificates and content hosting, all nine operations working with the AS listing paths instead of identifiers; the Release 19 Mas_Configuration API (TS 26.512 V19.3.0 clause 9) is absent on both sides.

requirements.name: M3 client in the AF, checked against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause governs M3 in Release 17)

cases.what: Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): before pushing anything to an AS, the AF fetches the list of certificates the AS already holds and stores it as the current state.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): the AF fetches the list of Content Hosting Configurations on the AS and records each entry as a provisioning session identifier.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): a certificate the AS does not yet hold is sent as a PEM bundle (application/x-pem-file) with POST; 201 removes it from the upload queue and the listed error codes are logged.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): a certificate the AS already holds is replaced with PUT; 200 and 204 are both treated as success.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): certificates queued for removal are deleted with DELETE; on 204 the AF drops them from its view of the AS.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): a Content Hosting Configuration the AS does not yet hold is sent as JSON with POST, with certificate references rewritten to the AF-unique certificate identifiers; 201 completes the upload.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): a configuration the AS already holds is replaced with PUT; 200 and 204 are both treated as success.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): configurations queued for removal are deleted with DELETE; on 204 the AF drops them from its view of the AS.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): a purge requested at M1 is forwarded to each AS as a form-encoded POST, with or without a pattern; 200 (with a purged-entry count) and 204 are both handled and the outcome is reported back to the M1 caller.

noted: No 3GPP clause governs this interface in Release 17: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 9 states "APIs of this reference point are not specified within this release." Every case in this row is checked against 5G-MAG's own M3 definition (/3gpp-m3/v1), not against a 3GPP clause.

When the AS answers a destroy request with an error (for example 404, or 409 for a certificate still in use), the request stays at the head of the queue and the AF sends it again straight away, with no limit on retries.
The AF accepts enumeration entries either as bare identifiers or as resource paths, keeping the last path element.
The AF names certificates on M3 as "{provisioningSessionId}:{certificateId}" so that identifiers are unique across Provisioning Sessions.
The AF talks M3 to each configured AS one request at a time, driven by a queue per AS (certificates first, then configurations, then deletions, then purges).

requirements.name: M3 server in the AS, checked against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause governs M3 in Release 17)

cases.what: Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): returns a JSON array of resource paths (the request path plus each identifier); the 5G-MAG definition gives the array items as ResourceId, that is the identifiers themselves.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): accepts a PEM bundle as application/x-pem-file, answers 201 with a Location header, 405 if the certificate already exists and 415 for another media type.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): replaces the certificate and reloads the web proxy, answering 200; answers 204 if the contents are unchanged and 404 if the certificate is unknown.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): removes the certificate and answers 204; answers 404 if unknown and 409 if a Content Hosting Configuration still uses it.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): returns a JSON array of resource paths (the request path plus each provisioning session identifier); the 5G-MAG definition gives the array items as ResourceId.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): accepts a JSON Content Hosting Configuration, starts or reloads the web proxy and answers 201 with a Location header; 405 if one already exists for that Provisioning Session, 415 for a wrong media type or an unusable configuration.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): replaces the configuration and reloads the web proxy, answering 200; 204 if unchanged, 404 if unknown, 415 for an unusable configuration.
Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): removes the configuration and answers 204; 404 if unknown.

Against the 5G-MAG M3 definition (no 3GPP clause): accepts a form-encoded pattern (a regular expression), purges matching cache entries and answers 200 with the number purged, 204 if none matched, 400 for a bad pattern and 415 for another media type.

noted: No 3GPP clause governs this interface in Release 17: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 9 states "APIs of this reference point are not specified within this release." Every case in this row is checked against 5G-MAG's own M3 definition (/3gpp-m3/v1), not against a 3GPP clause.
A purge request without a pattern purges every cached entry for that Content Hosting Configuration.
An unchanged Content Hosting Configuration update is answered 204 through the error path, so the 204 is built with a problem+json body.
Content Hosting Configurations are keyed by the provisioning session identifier, so the AS holds at most one per Provisioning Session.
The M3 server is generated from a merged 5G-MAG definition titled "Prototype 5GMS AS M3 API", version 0.0.0.
